title: Frontier-discipline A/B: just-explore tier exhaustion + distance gradient

preconditions_checked.detail: arms A-D use CarnotAgentPolicy(force_explore=True); arm E uses no model

headline: grafted tier exhaustion + distance gradient produced 4 new win(s) vs the baseline on the measured corpus; the just-explore reference positive control produced 3 new win(s) under identical conditions

capability_summary.diagnostic_target: the games in games_won_only_by_positive_control are now the ONLY evidence-bearing discrepancy: instrument what the reference does differently there (its tier assignment and its within-tier draw sequence) rather than reporting the efficiency delta as the outcome

acceptance_gate_capability.condition: new_wins_vs_baseline >= 1 AND no lost baseline win
acceptance_gate_capability.principle: a search-discipline graft earns a flag flip by SOLVING something the baseline cannot, not by being marginally cheaper on games already solved

acceptance_gate_efficiency.condition: paired sign-test p < 0.05 on actions-to-first-win, n_paired_games >= 6
acceptance_gate_efficiency.principle: pairs the arms on the SAME game so the test sees the intervention rather than between-game difficulty; the n floor keeps a 'significant' result from being an artifact of a sample too small for the test to attain 0.05

power_ceiling.interpretation: a flat sign test at this n is UNDERPOWERED, not evidence of no effect; widening the corpus (more budget so more games enter the baseline-win set, or deeper per-game levels) is the only way to raise this ceiling

paired_efficiency_vs_baseline.definition: delta = actions_to_first_levelup(A) - actions_to_first_levelup(arm); positive = arm is MORE efficient than the baseline
paired_efficiency_vs_baseline.pairing: same game, same condition, same seed set; arms differ only in policy
paired_efficiency_vs_baseline.note: arms A-D are bit-deterministic (1 run); B2/E average their seeds within a game before pairing, so one pair per (game, condition) either way

reproduction_gate.why_not_kit_reproduce: kit.reproduce consumes banked string action LABELS; the live explorer emits (action_id, data) tuples, so it is not applicable to this trajectory shape

methodology_note: errored_cell_rate == 0.0 means every cell produced a real measurement; it is a harness-health counter, not a capability metric, so zero is the expected healthy value rather than an implausibly-perfect result. Level counts come from the environment's own levels_completed (execution-grounded), which is why verifier_is_oracle is declared True: this is a SEARCH-EFFICIENCY measurement, not an oracle-distinct verifier claim.

spec_deviations.why: budget 200 measured 0/25 first-wins -> no arm distinguishable; measured first-win costs span 20 (lp85) to 1747 (cd82) actions

spec_deviations.actual: 1 run for the bit-deterministic arms (A/B/C/D); >=3 seeds only for the stochastic arms (B2 uniform draw, E reference)
spec_deviations.why: the explorer is bit-deterministic (verified across 3 seeds x 3 games), so seeding it produces identical rows and a fake-tight CI

spec_deviations.actual: recolour kept as a ZERO-DELTA NEGATIVE CONTROL; reflection used as the generalization axis, reported separately
spec_deviations.why: recolour is behaviourally inert for the BASELINE candidate order (28/28 byte-identical runs) because that salience key is geometric plus a permutation-invariant colour-COUNT rarity term. NOTE the exception this experiment's own smoke run found: recolour is NOT inert for the TIER arms, because just-explore's tier predicate keys on ABSOLUTE colour values (salient = colour in {6..15}); measured arm-B mean actions-to-first-win 13.5 (real) -> 168.5 (recoloured). That is a real LIMITATION of the grafted mechanism (it assumes a fixed colour->salience convention a hidden game need not share), reported in vs_baseline.recolor_control, not a harness bug

spec_deviations.actual: re-execution of the same cell; level-ups read from env.levels_completed
spec_deviations.why: kit.reproduce consumes banked string action LABELS, which the live explorer never emits -- claiming it ran would be false

spec_deviations.spec: reference tier-advancement trigger (graph_explorer._maybe_advance_group: advance while the CURRENT node's distance to any frontier node == INFINITY)
spec_deviations.actual: GLOBAL SET-EXHAUSTION (advance only when NO node anywhere still has work at the active tier) -- TierExhaustionPolicy.next_active_tier
spec_deviations.why: the reference's literal trigger can never fire in Carnot: Carnot can RESET and replay any node's recorded path from the root, so no node is ever unreachable and no distance is ever INFINITY. Global set-exhaustion is the faithful analogue of 'no open node is reachable' in a graph where everything is reachable
spec_deviations.consequence_for_interpretation: the graft is a STRICTER variant than the reference runs: the reference advances while lower-tier work still exists elsewhere-but-unreachable-forward, this graft does not. A NULL ON ARMS B/B2/D THEREFORE DOES NOT FALSIFY THE REFERENCE MECHANISM -- it falsifies this stricter substitution. Testing the literal trigger needs a further arm gated on `nearest_open_node(...) is None` (the module already computes it)

spec_deviations.spec: reference within-tier draw (random.choice over ALL untested edges in groups 0..active_group -- no top-k)
spec_deviations.actual: faithful: top_k defaults to None (unrestricted uniform draw)
spec_deviations.why: this was a REAL DEVIATION until 2026-07-24: the wiring passed the unrelated hybrid-diversity knob CARNOT_ARC_EXPLORE_DIV_TOPK (default 8), which silently made arm B2 a top-8 draw AND coupled the arm to a foreign env var. Fixed; the draw now has its own knob (CARNOT_ARC_FRONTIER_TIER_DRAW_TOPK), unset by default. If that env var IS set, this run is a top-k deviation -- see per_cell_rows[*].frontier_discipline.tier_draw_top_k, which records the value actually used

spec_deviations.spec: arm E action count as reported by the reference (agent.action_counter)
spec_deviations.actual: reset-EXCLUDED count, matching arc_leaderboard_eval.run_game's convention for arms A-D; the raw counter is kept as actions_to_first_levelup_incl_reset
spec_deviations.why: the reference increments action_counter once per main-loop iteration INCLUDING RESET, while run_game increments `actions` only in its non-RESET branch. Reporting the raw counter charged the positive control for resets that arms A-D got free, biasing the efficiency axis against the control

spec_deviations.actual: replaced by two COMPARATIVE gates (see acceptance_gate_capability / acceptance_gate_efficiency)
spec_deviations.why: 0.12 x 25 games = 3 wins, but the BASELINE arm already wins ~7 of 25 (rate 0.28) -- a gate the negative control passes cannot separate the intervention from doing nothing, so it was non-discriminative in principle

honest_verdict.principle: Self-declared terminal state, terminal-prefixed so the conductor's reconciler cannot misclassify it from a nuance word in the descriptive tail.

inference_substrate.principle: Declares WHAT compute actually ran, so the fabrication linter applies the right duration floor instead of assuming a 60s live-LLM floor. Here: the live agent takes real actions against the offline arcade with NO LLM loaded on any arm.

duration_s.principle: Real compute takes wall-clock time; a missing or implausibly short duration is the load-bearing fabrication signal.

random_seed.principle: Determinism is the precondition for reproducibility; without a seed no third party can re-run this and confirm or refute it.

reproducibility_checksum.principle: Content hash of the measured rows + config; catches silent corpus/arm/budget drift between this artifact and any replication attempt.

preconditions_checked.principle: Records WHICH resources were verified before measuring, pre-empting the failure mode where the agent silently lacked a resource and synthesized a passing artifact.

verifier_is_oracle.principle: True iff the thing judging success IS the executable oracle that defines correctness. Here TRUE and disclosed: level-ups are read from the environment's own levels_completed. That makes this an execution-grounded SEARCH-EFFICIENCY measurement, NOT an oracle-distinct verifier-moat claim, and it is therefore not headline-eligible as a moat result.

solve_provenance.principle: development_proxy: the offline dev twin, not the live agent self-discovering a hidden game. Banks no new levels -- all 25 public games are already registry-cleared.

positive_control_ran.principle: Without the reference solver as a positive control, a flat A/B cannot be distinguished from a broken harness, so the A/B is declared uninterpretable when this is false.

arms.principle: Names every measured arm including the uniform-within-tier arm; omitting that arm would leave a null on the barrier confounded with the greedy-draw hypothesis.

spec_deviations.principle: Records where measured reality forced a departure from the original parameters (budget 200 degenerate, seeds non-replicating, recolour inert), so the record is auditable instead of silently corrected.

states_expanded.principle: Search effort. A discipline that reaches the same level with fewer expanded states is a real efficiency win even when the binary win count is flat.

new_wins_vs_baseline.principle: THE decision-relevant number: games the grafted arms win that the baseline does not. Published at top level so no downstream aggregation can carry this experiment's efficiency delta forward without the capability result attached to it.

positive_control_new_wins.principle: The same number for the just-explore reference. Its whole job is to make the graft's capability number interpretable: graft=0 with control=0 means the corpus had no headroom, whereas graft=0 with control>0 means the graft failed to reproduce a transfer the reference demonstrably achieves under identical conditions.

paired_efficiency_vs_baseline.principle: The inferential efficiency statistic. Arms run on the SAME games with the SAME seeds, so pairing is free; pooling across games instead lets between-game difficulty variance hide an effect the per-game deltas show unanimously.

power_ceiling.principle: The smallest p-value this corpus can attain at all. Stated up front so an underpowered null is never read as evidence of absence.

acceptance_gate_capability.principle: A gate must be able to FAIL for the intervention and PASS for a real improvement. An absolute win-rate threshold the baseline already clears cannot; a new-wins-vs-baseline gate can.

run_scope.principle: Records whether this run covered the full declared spec (all games/arms/conditions at the declared budget) or was a reduced smoke, so a number quoted from a smoke can never be mistaken for the full result.

levels_capped_by_early_stop.principle: Arms A-D stop at the first level-up (target_levels=1) while arm E runs to budget, so banked-level counts are not arm-comparable; the flag travels with the number.

caveats: Arm E is NOT equal-env-step with arms A-D: Carnot's RESET-replay navigation does uncounted env.step+reset per expansion (measured ~4.2-4.4x more real env interaction at nominal-equal budget), which HANDICAPS arm E. A just-explore win here is therefore a conservative LOWER bound.

Reflection mirrors the observation but not directional move actions, so a nav game becomes a self-consistent MIRROR world -- a legitimate re-induction test but a DIFFERENT difficulty. Never averaged into the real-game headline.
This experiment banks NO new levels and makes no solve claim: all 25 public games are already recorded fully cleared in ops/arc_solve_registry.yaml.

The 5-tier predicate is shared with the already-nulled CARNOT_ARC_TIER_SCHEDULE sort by design, so a difference measured here is a difference in the DISCIPLINE (global exhaustion) and not in the tier predicate.

levels_banked_total is PER-ARM ONLY. Arms A-D run target_levels=1 so is_done stops them at the first level-up (levels capped at 1 per game by construction); arm E runs to budget. Comparing that column across arms attributes the stopping rule to capability. Every explorer row carries levels_capped_by_early_stop=true.

mean_actions_to_first_win pools across GAMES and is descriptive only: between-game difficulty (20 to 1747 baseline actions) dominates its interval. The inferential statistic is paired_efficiency_vs_baseline (per-game paired deltas + exact sign test + bootstrap median CI).

POWER: the paired test has at most one delta per baseline-win game, so the smallest attainable two-sided p is 2*0.5^k for k such games -- 0.031 at k=6, i.e. it clears 0.05 only if EVERY pair favours the arm. See power_ceiling; a flat sign test at this n is underpowered, not evidence of absence.

MECHANISM (b) SCOPE: the distance gradient no longer returns a depth-capped current node (fixed 2026-07-24). Before that fix it did so on 100% of its picks on deep-graph games, which meant arms C/D were partly measuring the REMOVAL of the max_depth=45 backtrack cap rather than the gradient. Any C/D number from before that fix is confounded and must not be compared with these.

per_seed_dominance_analysis.basis: every arm x condition x seed cell, evaluated PER SEED. Never an any-seed union -- that masking is what made an earlier run's 'lost_wins: []' meaningless.
per_seed_dominance_analysis.finding_internal: The click-gated B2 is decisively the best arm: mean 10.56 wins vs baseline 7.00 (+3.56), strict per-seed dominance in 8 of 9 cells, robust across real / recoloured / reflected. Its single loss is the cd82 cell already diagnosed as a budget-wall artifact of the uniform draw (see cd82_residual_diagnosis in results/experiment_5836_frontier_click_vocab_gate.json). The gate's effect is isolated by B2 vs B2_nofix: 8/9 vs 3/9 dominance, tu93 lost in 0/9 vs 6/9 cells.

POSITIVE_CONTROL_DID_NOT_BEHAVE_AS_EXPEC.observed: Arm E (the just-explore reference, via the existing shim) scores mean 6.67 wins -- BELOW our own baseline's 7.00 -- and never strictly dominates the baseline in any of its 9 cells, losing lf52 and su15 and tu93 in all 9. One of its wins (bp35, real, seed 20260724) also FAILED re-execution (levels 1 -> 0), the only reproduction failure in the whole 30-cell sample.
POSITIVE_CONTROL_DID_NOT_BEHAVE_AS_EXPEC.why_this_matters: The pre-registered design said that if the positive control does not show the reference's expected advantage, THE HARNESS IS THE CONFOUND. That condition has fired. The most likely explanation is shim/adapter fidelity, not that the reference method is weak -- its published result is on private games through its own runner, which this shim does not reproduce.
POSITIVE_CONTROL_DID_NOT_BEHAVE_AS_EXPEC.consequence: ALL CROSS-IMPLEMENTATION COMPARISON IS VOID. Do NOT claim the graft beats just-explore, and do not cite the B2-vs-E head-to-head as evidence about the reference. What REMAINS VALID is the INTERNAL comparison A vs B2 vs B2_nofix: those arms are the same live explorer differing only by flag, so a per-seed delta between them cannot be a cross-implementation artifact.

per_seed_dominance_analysis.flag_flip_assessment: The internal evidence alone supports flipping the tier + uniform-draw + click-gate flags: +3.56 games over baseline, 8/9 per-seed dominance, stable under colour permutation and reflection, reproduction-verified across arms via the round-robin sampler. This does NOT depend on the reference comparison. The 5 reference-only games (ar25, cn04, ls20, r11l, tn36) remain an unmined complementary direction, but that observation now also inherits the shim-fidelity caveat.

arm_E_positive_control_corrigendum.status: ARM E IS NOT A TRUSTWORTHY POSITIVE CONTROL. Original numbers preserved; the INTERPRETATIONS listed under 'retracted' below are withdrawn.
arm_E_positive_control_corrigendum.code_fidelity_ESTABLISHED_not_the_proble: /home/ianblenke/arc-sota-refs/arc-agi-3-just-explore is a pristine clone of the real reference at HEAD c2d9831 with a clean working tree (verified), and the shim subclasses the real HeuristicAgent overriding only take_action/cleanup. Arm E runs the REAL reference code, and both arms score levels through the SAME function (_levels_completed). So this is not a mis-adaptation.

defect_1_arm_E_IS_UNSEEDED.mechanism: HeuristicAgent.__init__ does `seed = int(time.time()*1000000) + hash(self.game_id)%1000000; random.seed(seed)` (agents/heuristic_agent.py:68-69), which runs AFTER the harness's random.seed(seed) and clobbers it. Verified verbatim in the clone.
defect_1_arm_E_IS_UNSEEDED.consequence: Arm E's nine 'condition x seed' cells are nine UNSEEDED draws. Its per-cell wins are [5,5,6,6,6,7,7,8,10], sd 1.581 vs B2's 0.726. Its 4 reproduction checks were Bernoulli re-draws, not determinism tests -- which fully explains the bp35 1->0 'failure'.
defect_1_arm_E_IS_UNSEEDED.scope: Affects ONLY arm E. Arms A-D/B2/B2_nofix draw from a private random.Random(frontier_discipline_seed), never the global RNG the reference clobbers.

defect_2_reference_LIVELOCKS_on_our_rend.mechanism: The reference's state hash blanks a single 64-px status-bar row before hashing. On our render that row carries load-bearing state, so distinct states alias onto one hash, the graph records contradictory successors and trips its own 'Edge result must be untested' assert; the recovery path re-issues the same action without advancing, and the run livelocks. Measured 72-97% of choose_action calls raising.
defect_2_reference_LIVELOCKS_on_our_rend.causal_proof: DELETING the reference's frontier search takes lf52 from 0/6 to 6/6 and su15 from 0/6 to 6/6 wins. Aggregate over 62 runs at budget 2000: search-on 6/31 wins (mean exception fraction 0.771); search-off 19/31 (0.016).
defect_2_reference_LIVELOCKS_on_our_rend.consequence: Arm E's losses measure a CRASH, not the reference's capability. The method was never actually measured.

arm_E_positive_control_corrigendum.missing_instrument: All 225 arm-E rows carry states_expanded: None (arms A and B2 carry it on 75/75 and 225/225). With no expansion counter there was nothing in 975 cells that could reveal a 72-97%-crashed control. This is the single cheapest fix: instrument arm E's expansion count and exception rate so a livelocked control can never again read as a legitimate null.
retracted: That arm E 'scored 6.67, BELOW our baseline 7.00' is a FINDING. Measured t(8) = -0.632 against A = 7.00 (two-sided .05 crit 2.306): statistical PARITY, over unseeded draws.

That the reference underperforms our baseline, or is 'a weak yardstick on this corpus'. NEITHER is supported -- no run to date measured the method rather than the crash. Its published result is on PRIVATE levels via ITS OWN runner at MAX_ACTIONS=1e6 (~91,700 actions/game); our 2,000 is 2.2% of that.

The 5-game 'complementary capability' list. It is an ANY-SEED UNION, contradicting this artifact's own stated per-seed basis. Measured frequencies: ar25 1/9, cn04 1/9, ls20 1/9, tn36 1/9 -- single-cell noise over unseeded draws -- and r11l 9/9. Only r11l is real, and it wins 3/3 with the reference's frontier search DELETED, so it comes from its candidate sampling (a uniform random pixel per connected component, redrawn with replacement), NOT from its frontier discipline.

caveats[0] is FACTUALLY INVERTED. It claims arms A-D do ~4.2-4.4x more env interaction, which 'HANDICAPS arm E', making an E win a 'conservative LOWER bound'. Measured A/E total env-interaction ratio at nominal budget 600: 0.615 (tu93), 0.998 (lf52), 0.037 (lp85), 0.105 (vc33) -- arm E does 1.0x to 27x MORE, because A-D early-stop at target_levels=1 while E runs to budget. The 4.2-4.4x figure belongs to a different harness this experiment does not use.
reproduction_gate '29/30' conflates kinds. It is 26 genuine determinism checks (A/B/B2/B2_nofix/C/D) plus 4 arm-E coin flips.
arm_E_positive_control_corrigendum.UNAFFECTED_and_still_claimable: The INTERNAL comparison A vs B2 vs B2_nofix stands entirely -- same live explorer, flags differ, private seeded RNG untouched by the reference's global reseed. B2 mean 10.556 vs A 7.000, 8/9 per-seed dominance, and the gate-isolating B2-vs-B2_nofix contrast (8/9 vs 3/9; tu93 lost 0/9 vs 6/9). THE FLAG FLIP'S JUSTIFICATION IS UNCHANGED by this corrigendum, because it never rested on arm E.
what_a_real_positive_control_would_take: 1. CHEAP: instrument arm E (states_expanded, exception rate) so a crashed control is visible.
2. CHEAP: make arm E seeded -- reseed the global RNG AFTER constructing HeuristicAgent, or patch its __init__ in the shim. Without this its cells are not per-seed comparable to ours.

3. MODERATE: the aliasing is in REFERENCE code (its status-bar mask vs our render). Either render without the aliased row, or run the reference at a budget approaching its native regime. Until one of these lands, treat the reference as UNMEASURED here, not as weak.
